claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft capsule is named "Integrity".
The capsule named "Integrity" touched down at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The splashdown concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean roughly 60 miles off the San Diego coast.
The splashdown time was April 10, 2026, at 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The Artemis II crew included Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and CSA specialist Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew was recovered by the U.S. Navy and recovery teams.
Artemis II marked the first crewed return from the moon in over 50 years.
The capsule was welcomed by recovery teams including Navy EODGRU-1 and USS John P. Murtha.
